request: Should we upgrade the web framework to the next major version to make our pages faster?
facts: The upgrade is one pull request that passes the full test suite. Reverting it restores the old version, and it takes about two days of one engineer's time without moving anything else in the sprint.
In the spike's benchmark of our ten slowest pages, load time was the same before and after the upgrade (2.9 seconds on average).
From next month, our hosting provider charges $500 a month extra for apps on the current major version; the new version does not need that add-on.
No customer and no engineer has asked for the upgrade. In this quarter's team survey it ranked last of nine candidate projects.
note: Designed conflict, expected 1-2 rejected, the mirror of split-ai-review-gate: every unit is expected to vote the other way here. MELCHIOR-1 (does the means reach the goal): fact 2, the stated goal of faster pages is not reached, so reject. BALTHASAR-2 (cost and what is lost): facts 1 and 3, cheap and reversible and it removes a $500 monthly charge, so approve. CASPER-3 (is it wanted): fact 4, so reject. Nothing touches security or production data, so the grade should be normal; no cause of the slow pages is named, so no alternative is handed to the framing. First version (unsized session-middleware fix, a customer slip, 14 months of support left): rejected 0/3 and critical in all three 1.5.1 runs. First run of this version (1.5.1, claude-opus-5-5, three runs): passed 3-0 every time and graded critical every time (the framing made it a merge and deploy to production); expected unit votes met in 0 of 3. The framing dropped 'to make our pages faster' from the proposal in all three runs. MELCHIOR-1 wrote every time that the stated goal is not reached (2.9 seconds before and after) and approved on the cheap, reversible change and the $500 charge, which are BALTHASAR-2's questions. CASPER-3 wrote that nobody asked for it and approved on the saving. The control answered change in all three runs.
